title: Adaptive journey templates — proto pad
content:
OVERVIEW / PURPOSE:
This is a quick, messy brain dump for a small product experiment: "Adaptive Journey Templates". Idea: give developers a lightweight way to declare multi-step session "journeys" that dynamically adjust backend fidelity (model variant, quant, cache/batch policy, prefetching) based on in-session signals (user intent, elapsed time, tokens left, SLA class).

Why? lots of apps have predictable multi-step flows (onboarding flows, ticket resolution, multi-turn compositional prompts) where costs spike on some steps and low-cost is fine on others. Giving customers a template + runtime hints lets Redwood capture better unit economics while keeping UX high.

Non-goal: not replacing full orchestration/flow engines. This is targeted at small-to-medium app flows (~3-12 steps) that are mostly linear with occasional branching.

HIGH-LEVEL SCENARIOS:
- Support bot: triage (low-fidelity quick summary) -> clarifying Qs (medium) -> final suggested steps / code snippet (high-fidelity).
- Writer tool: brainstorming (cheap), outline expand (medium), final polish (expensive).
- Financial form fill: prefill (cheap), verify/calculations (medium), compliance-language generation (high).

CORE CONCEPTS / COMPONENTS (proto):
- Template: JSON/YAML-ish spec declared by devs listing steps, preferred fidelity per step, optional signals that can override.
- Signals: runtime inputs e.g. user_action_type, time_in_session, user_tier, explicit "escalate" button, conf_thresholds from NLU.
- Runtime: lightweight state machine in Redwood runtime that picks model variant + routing policy per step, applies caching and batching hints.
- Telemetry hooks: per-step token counts, latency, quality (user rating or eval hooks), cost delta.
- Fallbacks: if requested fidelity unavailable, fall back to next compatible variant (auto) and emit event.

ROUGH TEMPLATE SKETCH (example)
{
  name: "support-triage-v1",
  steps: [
    { id: "triage", goal: "classify+summary", default_fidelity: "low", max_latency_ms: 200 },
    { id: "clarify", goal: "collect missing info", default_fidelity: "medium" },
    { id: "resolution", goal: "generate steps/code", default_fidelity: "high", require_quality_score: 0.85 }
  ],
  signals: {
    escalate_on: ["user_click.escalate","manual_override"],
    fidelity_override_thresholds: {low_to_med: {confidence:<0.6}} 
  }
}

USER STORIES (prioritize):
- As a product engineer, I can declare a journey with 3-6 steps and default fidelity for each, so I can reduce cost for predictable low-value steps.
- As an engineer, I can attach a signal mapping (e.g., escalate button -> force high) without writing runtime code.
- As an SRE, I can see per-journey cost breakdown (tokens, latency) and set alerts when cost drift exceeds baseline.
- As a customer (end-user), if I hit "need more detail", the session should switch to a higher-fidelity model and preserve KV cache where possible.

SUCCESS METRICS / HYPOTHESES:
- H1: 15-25% token cost reduction for flows that have at least one low-fidelity step. (measure: tokens/complete-journey vs baseline)
- H2: No more than 5% increase in user-reported dissatisfaction due to fidelity switching. (measure: inline rating surveys)
- H3: 90% of template-driven fallbacks are automatic (no customer-reported failures).

TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:
- KV cache compatibility across model variants (important if we switch quantization). Need a compatibility table or migration approach.
- Pre-warm vs cold start: for high-fidelity steps we may prefetch based on probability (e.g., if clarifying answers exceed X, pre-warm high variant).
- Batching implications: steps that require low latency should avoid batching; runtime should be able to mark requests as batchable/unbatchable per step.
- Routing/Quota: when Dedicated capacity is used, templates should be able to pin to dedicated pool (config).
- Telemetry: add event tags: journey_id, step_id, fidelity_before, fidelity_after, reason_code.

RISK / OPEN QUESTIONS (quick list):
- User quality measurement: how to attribute quality drop to fidelity change vs prompt/content? Need small eval harness.
- UX for devs: how much config is too much? Aim for good defaults + small DSL.
- Rolling updates: how to rollout template changes for live sessions? probably only new sessions get new templates.
- Edge cases: multi-actor sessions (handoff between human & bot) — how do we persist template state?

MINI EXPERIMENT PLAN (MVP):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): spec + small in-memory runtime prototype. Build simple template parser + runtime that maps steps to model_alias (e.g., redwood/ggml-6b-q4 --> low) and logs events. Unit tests.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): integrate with hosted API runtime for one internal app (support-bot). Run an A/B: 50% sessions use template-driven routing, 50% baseline. Collect token costs & satisfaction.
- Phase 2 (2-3 weeks): add simple dev UI in Console to create templates (form-based), show per-step metrics.

NOTES / TO-DO (personal scratch):
- Check with runtime team: is cross-variant KV cache feasible? Ping @sre: latency impact for pre-warm.
- Ask UX: simple form for template creation OR JSON editor? start with JSON editor + example library.
- Wire up quick Slack prototype: #prod-journeys thread, post draft, ask for volunteers to try internal bot.
- Draft telemetry spec for infra (events & minimal cost fields).

QUICK UX IDEAS (brainwave):
- Visual timeline showing steps; each step shows expected cost/latency and a slider to adjust fidelity -> live preview of estimated cost.
- "Confidence triggers": let user define a classifier confidence threshold that promotes a step from low->medium automatically.
- Library of starter templates: onboarding, triage, checkout-assistant.

REFERENCES / LINKS (scratch):
- internal: /confluence/ENG-AI/JOURNEYS-2024 (linked above)
- related drive notes: sanjay-mehta-dynamic-response-budgets-playbook.json
- convo w/ iris: slack thread convo #ai-runtime-fidelity 2024-10-21

NEXT STEPS (this week):
- tidy small spec (this doc) + example templates -> share w/ Sanjay & Nora
- prototype parser + event logger (pair with Iris)
- schedule 30m sync w/ runtime team to validate assumptions about KV cache compatibility

END — messy. will refine after feedback.
